Let's break down the core architecture and features so you can fully understand the scope before writing any code.

5. The Employee Portal & File Management

The employee portal needs to handle daily check-ins and heavy file uploads (PDFs, DOCX, ZIP files).

Because saving large ZIP files directly to a PostgreSQL database is inefficient, you should use an Object Storage bucket (like AWS S3 or Supabase Storage).

7. The AI Summarization Engine (The RAG Pipeline)

t of your project. When the Superadmin or Admin clicks on an employee's name, they shouldn't have to read through 20 daily PDF reports.

Here is how you build the AI summarization feature:

Data Extraction: When an employee uploads a PDF or DOCX report, a backend script (using a library like PyPDF2) immediately extracts the raw text.

Vectorization (Chroma/Supabase pgvector): The text is chunked and stored in your vector database.

The Admin Trigger: When the Admin clicks "Generate Summary" on the employee's profile, your API makes a query: "Fetch all reports from [Employee Name] for the last

e, your API makes a query: "Fetch all reports from [Employee Name] for the last 7 days."

LLM Generation: The retrieved text is passed to an LLM (via an API like OpenRouter) with a system prompt: "Summarize this researcher's weekly progress, highlight any blockers, and list their completed tasks."

Output: The Superadmin sees a clean, bulleted AI summary generated in seconds.
